checks.Title: Seduce, don't just observe
checks.Evidence: The prose lingers on seductive-strange textures before horror arrives: the harrower's voice 'arrived the way a draft arrives through a door you hadn't noticed was open,' the membrane described as 'a gift nobody had asked it to stop giving,' and the tactile detail of frost that 'never burned off' at the treeline, plus the lived-in wrongness of a leashed sinterspawn trained to 'go home.'

checks.Title: Open with the world doing its work
checks.Evidence: The opening paragraph does establish Aldford as a village that 'existed because the ford did' with garrison watch fires and villagers who don't call the wilds by their true name, and there is a brief village-life beat (marigold crowns, the Crowning ritual, Sage's transaction with Lyra) before the plot intrudes with the runner reporting Heather missing — but this grounding stretch is quite short (roughly five paragraphs) before machinery kicks in.
checks.Fix: Extend the pre-plot village texture by another beat or two — e.g., linger longer on ordinary market/garrison routine or another villager's unremarkable errand — so the seduction of the world is fully earned before the disappearance derails it.

checks.Title: Gloss first mentions in-voice, never dump
checks.Evidence: Terms like 'the Untamed', 'sinterspawn', 'membrane', 'kin-pack', 'harrower', and 'the Old Watch manuals' are mostly glossed well in-voice (e.g., 'called what began on the far bank the Untamed - plainly, the way you'd name a dog you didn't trust'), but 'CorpoNations'-style proprietary worldbuilding is absent and some terms like 'sinterspawn' and 'membrane-heavy tissue' arrive with technical density ('the membrane has replaced the biology with something it didn't bother to translate cleanly') that reads more like lore-exposition than a Templar's natural voice.
checks.Fix: Trim the clinical membrane/biology explanation to a shorter sensory beat consistent with Lyra's practical, embodied POV, and give 'sinterspawn' the same light in-voice anchoring the other terms receive.

checks.Title: Never an acronym before its term
checks.Evidence: The story contains no acronyms at all (terms like 'kin-pack', 'harrower', 'sinterspawn', and 'membrane' are used as plain nouns, never abbreviated), so the commandment about gating acronyms behind their expansion has nothing to violate.

checks.Title: Give the POV character one human crack
checks.Evidence: The thanking of Sage 'the way she'd once thanked Vega, badly, over ruined marigolds in a kitchen garden three hundred miles and a lifetime from any ford' is the one flash of a prior human self, but it's delivered in a single subordinate clause and immediately folded back into her competence ('with the same specific gravity she'd have used thanking a superior officer').
checks.Fix: Let the Vega memory land for one more beat—a half-sentence of what was lost or why it still surfaces—before she re-armors into the officer register.

checks.Title: Land one beat past the handoff
checks.Evidence: The plot business (the lie to the Marshes, the coverup, the harrower's head hitting the yard) resolves cleanly, and the final beat—'Write it up,' and she went inside—reads as closure rather than an added quiet gesture; the Corwin thread is noticed but explicitly shelved ('She set it aside... let him keep his correct, empty face'), which gestures at 'what happens in this city' but doesn't land a final image carrying cost the way Sage's crown might have.
checks.Fix: End instead on a single wordless image—Lyra finally freeing Sage's crushed crown from under her pauldron and setting it down rather than discarding it or reporting it—so the last beat is a private, physical gesture that carries the cost of the lie rather than the procedural line 'Write it up.'

checks.Title: Reward re-reading without requiring it
checks.Evidence: The Sage's-crown detail (given 'so the wolves don't get you,' then found crushed and blooded on the false trail, then revealed to be a decoy while Heather's real crown 'gone the whole way to Millbrook still on her head') and Corwin's repeated, unexplained glance toward the stableboy work perfectly on a first read as texture/misdirection, but both reread as planted clues to the story's actual mechanics once the reader knows Heather staged her death and Corwin has his own secret.

checks.Title: Elevate, don't reconstruct
checks.Evidence: The prose establishes world terms (harrowers, kin, the Untamed, membrane, sinterspawn, Old Watch manuals) through in-scene context and character action rather than exposition dumps, and the emotional/plot mechanics (Lyra's rank anxiety, Baast's grudge, Heather's fake death) are fully dramatized so a newcomer can follow without prior lore, while nothing about the scene structure reads as retrofitted signage for tourists.
